name: Primary Osteolysis

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of progressive bone resorption without an identifiable secondary cause
Exclusion of secondary causes of osteolysis such as infection, malignancy, or metabolic bone disease
Presence of localized bone pain, swelling, or deformity consistent with osteolytic lesions
Identification of mutations in genes associated with hereditary osteolysis (e.g., MMP2, MAFB) if available

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiologic evidence of osteolysis plus exclusion of secondary causes and compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

searchTerms: gradual bone loss in one area

common.symptomName: Reduced range of motion in adjacent joints

occasional.symptomName: Muscle weakness adjacent to affected bone
Nerve compression symptoms due to bone deformity
searchTerms: nerve pain from bone pressing on nerves
tingling or numbness due to bone deformity
nerve symptoms caused by bone changes
small red blood vessels on skin over bone loss
visible tiny blood vessels on skin near bone damage

rare.symptomName: Osteonecrosis secondary to extensive bone loss
searchTerms: bone tissue death due to bone loss
bone death from poor blood supply

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
Absence of markers indicating infection or malignancy
imaging: Progressive osteolytic lesions on X-ray or CT scan
MRI showing bone marrow changes without soft tissue mass
Bone scintigraphy showing increased uptake in affected areas
genetic: Mutations in MMP2 gene (associated with multicentric osteolysis)
Mutations in MAFB gene (associated with nodulosis and osteolysis)
other: Histopathology showing absence of neoplastic cells and presence of osteoclast-mediated bone resorption

distinguishingFeatures: Typically involves carpal and tarsal bones
Associated with nephropathy in some cases
Marked by massive osteolysis with lymphatic proliferation
Histology shows vascular or lymphatic proliferation

redFlags: Rapidly progressive bone loss leading to functional impairment
Neurological deficits due to nerve compression from bone deformity
references: Mumm S, et al. Hereditary multicentric osteolysis: clinical and genetic aspects. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 2007.
Radhakrishnan J, et al. Primary osteolysis: a review of pathogenesis and clinical features. J Bone Miner Res. 2019.
